metadata.title: The Bottom of a Rolling Wheel Is Completely Still
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: A wheel rolls forward without slipping. How fast is the point touching the ground moving?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: A wheel rolls along the ground without slipping. Follow a single point on its rim. That point sweeps out a looping arch called a cycloid, and each time it reaches the ground, its path comes to a sharp point. So how fast is the point touching the ground actually moving?
beats.new_visual_element: A bicycle-style wheel (black tire ring, grey spokes, hub) rolls left to right along a ground line; a gold dot on the rim leaves a dotted slate cycloid trail with one cusp at the ground.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: ground line, wheel at rest at the right after one revolution, cycloid trail with cusp

beats.narration_text: Rolling is two motions at once. First, translation: the whole wheel slides forward, and every point shares the velocity of the center, v. Second, rotation: the wheel spins about its center, and every point on the rim moves tangent to the circle with speed R omega.
beats.new_visual_element: Two panels (side by side in 16:9, stacked in 9:16). Translation panel: wheel with five identical teal arrows (center + four rim points) pointing right. Rotation panel: same wheel with crimson tangent arrows at four rim points in the clockwise sense, a dot at the center.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: translation panel (teal arrows, label v) and rotation panel (crimson arrows, label R omega)

beats.narration_text: Rolling without slipping ties the two together: the rim speed R omega equals the center speed v. Now add the two velocities at each point. At the top they point the same way, and the sum is two v. At the front they are perpendicular, and the sum points diagonally down. At the bottom they point in opposite directions, and they cancel exactly.
beats.new_visual_element: One wheel on the ground with header R omega = v. At top, front and bottom in turn: teal translation arrow and crimson rotation arrow, then the black resultant (2v at top, diagonal at front, zero at bottom marked with a ring).
beats.accumulated_scene_state: single wheel with black resultant arrows at top (2v) and front, and a ring with 0 at the contact point

beats.narration_text: Now let the wheel roll, with the resultant velocity drawn at eight points on the rim. Each point speeds up to two v as it passes over the top, then slows to exactly zero as it reaches the ground, and rises again. Whichever point is touching the ground is, at that instant, at rest.
beats.new_visual_element: The wheel rolls continuously; eight black resultant arrows fixed to rim points update every frame from v(1 + sin phi, -cos phi). A gold ring at the contact point brightens each time a marked point arrives there with zero velocity.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: rolling wheel with live resultant-arrow field, contact ring

beats.narration_text: Translation plus rotation. At the top they add to twice the speed of the center; at the bottom they cancel completely. The point of a rolling wheel that touches the ground is, for an instant, perfectly still.
beats.new_visual_element: Wheel stops; it dims to light grey except the top arrow labeled 2v and the contact ring labeled v = 0, which stay in full contrast.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: dimmed wheel, top 2v arrow, contact ring with v = 0
